subject: Materials Science
title: Graphene: The Wonder Material
description: A micro-lesson that makes Graphene: The Wonder Material usable.

hook.text: One atom thick, transparent, flexible, and stronger than diamond — graphene won the 2010 Nobel Prize in Physics.

buildup.text: Graphene is a single layer of carbon atoms in a hexagonal lattice — isolated from graphite with adhesive tape in 2004.

discovery.text: Electrons in graphene travel as massless Dirac fermions — reaching 1/300th the speed of light in the material.

twist.text: Graphene has no band gap — it can't be switched off, making it unsuitable for digital transistors without modification.

climax.text: Graphene excels in composites, coatings, sensors, and energy storage — even if the transistor dream stalled.

punchline.text: Thinnest, strongest, most conductive sheet — still seeking its killer app.

quiz.question: Why is graphene not widely used in digital transistors?
options: It is too expensive to produce
It has no band gap and cannot be switched off for logic operations
It breaks too easily at small sizes
